extracted.intended_audience: student journalists and high-school newspaper managers and staff
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and standards for creating, planning, placing, and accepting advertising for high-school (student) newspapers, including campaign planning, printed and oral ad technique, layout, sales operations, and ethical standards for accepting ads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five goals of a printed advertisement
rubrics_metrics.description: A good printed advertisement should make its public do five things: see, read, believe, remember, and act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design copy and art so the reader notices the ad (see), reads it, is convinced of its claim, remembers the product/name (e.g., via slogan), and is led to take action (buy, subscribe).

rubrics_metrics.name: Five goals of an oral advertisement
rubrics_metrics.description: The oral advertisement should make the public hear, listen, believe, remember, and act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For spoken appeals substitute hearing and listening techniques for visual devices; all other goals mirror printed advertising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make Him See / Catch attention
rubrics_metrics.description: Catch attention by the novelty of the headline; by suggestion; by a startling slogan; by a picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spectacular devices include moving electric signs, sky writing, neon signs; use novelty and striking visuals or phrasing to stop the eye.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold attention with concrete, vivid detail (Make Him Read)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once you have caught attention, hold it by sparkling concrete details that challenge the need and the imagination of the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal to an interest, emotion, attitude, instinct, the senses, reason, or a special point of view; use the new, strange, picturesque, unexpected, timeliness, dramatic form, the power of the particular and startling parallels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspire confidence (Make Him Believe)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inspire confidence by the sincerity of the advertisement and the advertiser’s thorough knowledge of the commodity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Devices include testimonials and guarantees; aim for a tone that makes readers feel 'He knows what he is talking about.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Make it memorable (Make Him Remember)
rubrics_metrics.description: By a slogan or catch phrase, preferably one that links the name of the firm with the commodity, make the commodity stick in the mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a concise linking phrase and sufficient repetition to build recall (examples: 'Fairy Soap'; 'All the news that’s fit to print').

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitate action (Make Him Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make it easy for him to act; show him how to get your commodity without inconvenience to himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider customer conditions (hours, location); provide easy payment plans; remove barriers that deter purchase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral technique — Make Him Hear
rubrics_metrics.description: By the novelty of the attack, pique his curiosity; a dramatic entrance or stage business may catch his ear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the right point of contact and opening device to secure the audience’s auditory attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral technique — Make Him Listen
rubrics_metrics.description: Once attention has been arrested, hold it through brief vivid details. Make no 'cotton wool statements.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a pleasing voice and manner, attention to the pause, force of personality; in personal appeals seize any clue revealing a customer's interest and tailor the message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan a general campaign (timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan a general campaign at the beginning of the term to sell term subscriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule a broad subscription push early; coordinate resources and messaging across term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan specific campaigns before each issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan specific campaigns before each issue to sell single copies to those who do not subscribe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify features of the upcoming issue to promote and run targeted short campaigns for single-issue sales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know your commodity
rubrics_metrics.description: Know your commodity—what your paper publishes, its distinctive points, offerings planned to meet student needs and special tastes; special talents on the staff; what some worth-while persons have said of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventory editorial strengths and unique selling points to use in sales pitches and copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know your public
rubrics_metrics.description: Know your public—student body, faculty, alumni. This knowledge must include the number of each group, and the total number of subscribers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather demographics and counts to target campaigns, set quotas, and evaluate reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set financial target
rubrics_metrics.description: Set yourself the sum needed to cover costs of publication for the term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute subscription revenue targets and budget to ensure the paper is financially viable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain detailed class rosters for sales
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide yourself with a roster of official classes showing class number, number of students on register, full names of teachers, full names of students, room number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use rosters to assign sales agents, distribute subscription cards, and check returns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare introductory letters to classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Draw up a sparkling letter to introduce the project to each class; state price and ask for appointment of a live sales agent; include a detachable stub for return.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mimeograph one letter per class; provide fill-in stub to capture class/agent/room info and set return deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare follow-up letter for agents to read
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan a special follow-up letter to be read later to each class by its special sales agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use scripted follow-up readings to reinforce the message and prompt commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan poster copy and order art early
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan copy for posters about the building and place your order with your art department well in advance of expected delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posters should show price; some should be targeted to boys or girls; large color posters are much more effective than small black-and-white; illustrations suggesting action are preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare and apply an assembly address
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare an address for your assembly applying the principles of good advertising; plan an attack that will make the student body hear you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use theatrical or newsboy devices (e.g., 'Extra! Extra!') to dramatize the pitch and secure attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide and manage numbered subscription receipt cards
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide headquarters with a sufficient number of subscription receipt cards, each bearing a number, sorted into packages matching class sizes and tracked at headquarters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbering and class assignment help with later reconciliation of sales and checking returns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call and instruct special sales agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a notice calling together your special sales agents; specify day, hour, place; provide them with letters and subscription cards and give a brief lesson in salesmanship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruct agents to begin sales at once, accept full or part payments (with part-payment cards held until paid), give receipts, report daily, and study their small group’s interests for tailored appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize headquarters to handle returns
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize a force at headquarters to handle returns as they come in; make it easy for special sales agents and customers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Having staff ready to receive payments and answer questions preserves confidence and prevents lost sales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stock back numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Get together enough back numbers to supply new entrants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure newcomers can still purchase earlier issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribute samples and posters during campaign
rubrics_metrics.description: During the general campaign distribute sample copies to new entrants and place posters about the building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical samples and visible posters reinforce messaging and create points of contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect stubs and ensure representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect stubs and check them with class lists; ensure one representative for each class and follow up immediately if any class lacks one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate remedial action maintains coverage and sales momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up and troubleshoot low-performing classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow up all responses; if some classes show little action discover the cause and remedy it; replace sales agents lacking initiative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagnose barriers (wrong agent, wrong time, bad pitch) and take corrective steps quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and publish results to stimulate rivalry
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize special ability in salesmen—praise them; recognize unusual responses in classes and publish results to stimulate interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use healthy competition (e.g., display ribbons or publish 100-percent classes) to drive sales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Run teasers and last calls
rubrics_metrics.description: Run teasers in your first issue—and a last call for subscriptions!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use editorial space to prompt immediate purchases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliver papers simultaneously
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver all papers to all parts of the school at the same time (including annexes where feasible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid offering news after students have already heard it elsewhere; simultaneous delivery preserves fairness and sales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet conditions and be available at launch
rubrics_metrics.description: Meet all conditions; make it possible for late comers to get papers; be on the job when the first paper comes out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early failures are hard to recover from; ensure logistics are handled before launch.

rubrics_metrics.name: After-campaign actions
rubrics_metrics.description: After the campaign take down all posters; be alive to comments on the paper; no post-mortems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect reader feedback for future improvements but avoid publicly dwelling on failures ('no post-mortems').

rubrics_metrics.name: Special single-issue campaign: know the distinctive features
rubrics_metrics.description: Before a single-issue campaign, know the distinctive features of the coming issue (e.g., exclusive exam schedule, celebrity interview) and plan copy/posters/address accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote specific, time-sensitive attractions to boost single-copy sales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special single-issue campaign: strategic placement and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: During single-issue campaigns place posters, address assemblies, use special sales agents for non-subscribing classes, cover strategic points, and be on time (early bird principle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position sellers at high-traffic strategic points to catch indifferent buyers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to advertisers: honor agreements and follow copy
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever agreement the paper makes with the advertiser must be kept unqualifiedly; editors must see that the printer follows copy rigidly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ad copy and display must be printed as contracted; 'follow copy even though it flies out the window.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid editorial contradiction of ads
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper must print no contradictions of the advertisements it carries (e.g., do not run editorials attacking patent medicines while carrying patent-medicine ads).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain consistency between editorial content and paid advertising commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to readers: accept only bona fide advertisements
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers must be protected against any but bona fide advertisements; high-standard papers back their advertisements and will knowingly give space to nothing of a doubtful nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screen advertisers to protect reader trust and editorial integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider ad in relation to whole page (page harmony)
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor’s problem is one of placing the advertisement on the page: consider the ad in relation to the whole page and in relation to other advertisements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ads must stand out without destroying harmony of page make-up; use variety of borders to avoid monotony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cuts should face in
rubrics_metrics.description: Cuts should face in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placement of illustrations/cuts should be oriented toward the page composition for better visual flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Space on back page is premium
rubrics_metrics.description: Space on the back page is more desirable from the advertiser's viewpoint than a similar position on an inside page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Back-page inventory can command higher rates; consider advertiser preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ads should be in tone with the paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertisements should be in tone with the paper; cheap advertising is the mark of a cheap paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose advertisers and ad creative that match the paper’s overall character and audience expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sell space by standard units and set fair rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Space should be sold by the column-inch, quarter-page, half-page; the rate should be determined by the cost of printing and include a fair margin of profit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard units for pricing and compute rates to cover costs and yield reasonable profit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan proportion of advertising to editorial matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The proportion of advertising matter to editorial matter should be carefully planned; students want the news of the community first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overloading pages with ads at the expense of core content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not solicit unknown firms without consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should not solicit advertisements from unknown firms or persons without the consent of their advisers or parents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect students and the paper from unscrupulous or risky solicitations by requiring adult oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitors must be informed about commodity and audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicitors should be well enough informed on their commodity, the paper, and their public to help prospective advertisers who may not know what appeal to make to high school students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train solicitors to propose effective ad approaches for the target student audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not sell space if circulation is too small
rubrics_metrics.description: If the paper does not reach a large number of students, space should not be sold; the selling of space is a business proposition—fairness works both ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect advertisers by ensuring adequate reach before accepting paid placements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising pictures should suggest action
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertising pictures, like newspaper cartoons, should suggest action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer dynamic imagery that implies movement or narrative to engage viewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posters should show price and target demographics
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertising posters should show price. Some should appeal to boys; some to girls, if the school is co-ed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor poster creative and information to the intended buyer segments; prioritize visibility and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise-based critique criteria for ads
rubrics_metrics.description: Ads that are not pleasing may suffer from: too many details; lack of emphasis; irrelevant details; lack of balance; unrelated picture and copy; incongruous pictorial effect; violation of truth; inaccuracies from a special viewpoint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this checklist to analyze weaknesses in ad composition, messaging, and ethical accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: New York Times: categories of advertising declined (summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: The New York Times declines certain classes of advertisements it regards as improper; the text lists specific categories that it will not publish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the NYT list as a model for types of ads a reputable paper should refuse; see the separate items for the full enumerated list.

rubrics_metrics.name: NYT decline: fraudulent or doubtful advertisements
rubrics_metrics.description: Decline fraudulent or doubtful advertisements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject ads that make patently false or deceptive promises or that are of questionable legitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: NYT decline: offers of something for nothing; false/exaggerated claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Decline offers of something of value for nothing; advertisements that make false, unwarranted or exaggerated claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screen for unrealistic 'free' offers and hyperbolic assertions unsupported by facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: NYT decline: ambiguous or misleading wording
rubrics_metrics.description: Decline advertisements that are ambiguous in wording and which may mislead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure ad copy is clear and not phrased to deceive by omission or ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: NYT decline: personal attacks on competitors
rubrics_metrics.description: Decline attacks of a personal character; advertisements that make uncalled-for reflections on competitors or competitive goods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid accepting ads that libel or gratuitously attack other businesses or individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: NYT decline: promising large guaranteed dividends or excessive profits
rubrics_metrics.description: Decline advertisements holding out the prospect of large guaranteed dividends or excessive profits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of investment or get-rich-quick offers promising unrealistic returns.

rubrics_metrics.name: NYT decline: bucket shops and undesirable financial firms
rubrics_metrics.description: Decline bucket shops and offerings of undesirable financial firms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screen financial advertisers for legitimacy and regulatory compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: NYT decline: indecent, vulgar, suggestive, repulsive or offensive ads
rubrics_metrics.description: Decline advertisements that are indecent, vulgar, suggestive, repulsive or offensive, either in theme or treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain standards of decency appropriate to the paper and its readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: NYT decline: matrimonial offers, fortune telling, unlicensed massage
rubrics_metrics.description: Decline matrimonial offers; fortune telling; massage, unless licensed and license number is given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refuse personal-ad categories or services with potential for fraud or requiring proof of licensing.

rubrics_metrics.name: NYT decline: objectionable medical advertising and unsupported remedial claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Decline objectionable medical advertising and offers of free medical treatment; advertising that makes remedial, relief or curative claims not justified by the facts or common experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require medical ads be factual, evidence-based, and not promise cures unsupported by reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: NYT decline: products with habit-forming or dangerous drugs
rubrics_metrics.description: Decline advertising of products containing habit-forming or dangerous drugs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject ads for controlled or hazardous substances.

rubrics_metrics.name: NYT decline: help-wanted ads requesting money for samples or articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Decline Help Wanted advertisements which request money for samples or articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect job-seekers from exploitative 'pay-to-apply' schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: NYT decline: any advertising causing money loss or injury to readers or regarded as unworthy
rubrics_metrics.description: Decline any other advertising that may cause money loss to the reader or injury in health or morals, or loss of confidence in reputable advertising and honorable business, or which is regarded by THE TIMES as unworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use broad editorial discretion to refuse ads likely to harm readers or the paper's reputation.
